description: Weekly batch: branches are created/updated only Monday before 06:00 LA time, which the renovate-ocidex CronJob in homelab (every 4h, America/Los_Angeles) hits at 00:00 and 04:00. Vulnerability alerts ignore the schedule. Every automerge is a push to main and a full push pipeline, so batching weekly keeps that to a few runs a week.

packageRules.description: Automerge minor, patch, digest and pin updates across all managers. vulnerabilityAlerts sets no automerge, so non-major security fixes inherit this too. Group rules below set groupName only — no automerge, so this rule remains the single source of truth for automerge. rebaseWhen 'conflicted' (top level) lets a green PR merge without first being rebased onto every new main commit, which would re-run the PR pipeline and push the merge to the next Renovate run.

Digest-pin runtime and build images so every build is reproducible and Renovate owns the rebase. Deliberately excludes the .tekton/ CI images: ghcr.io/pfenerty/apko-cicd/base:stable is a moving tag used 100+ times, so pinning it would force a Renovate PR plus a `make tekton-synth` on every upstream base rebuild.

Never pin or bump the images this repo builds itself: the charts take their tag from Chart.appVersion at package time. Pinning wrote the operator digest into image.tag as "@sha256:...", which rendered an unparseable reference (ocidex-35rx).
Chainguard publishes only :latest on the free tier, so the digest IS the version — and a new digest is usually the CVE fix we picked this image for. Skip the global 3-day hold.
Group all Go module updates into one PR

Go dev tools pinned in tools/go.mod (golangci-lint, sqlc, oapi-codegen, controller-gen, go-licenses, govulncheck) get their own PR: a linter or generator bump can turn main red or change generated code, so it shouldn't ride along with app dependency updates. postUpgradeTasks regenerates every codegen-check output, so a generator bump carries its own output instead of failing codegen-check (oapi-codegen v2.8.0 renamed enum constants; controller-gen stamps its version into the CRDs). Needs RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS to allow these commands and `make` in the Renovate image.

Group all .tektonic/ npm updates (@tektonic-ci/*, tsx, typescript, @types/node) into one branch, so the re-synth below runs once instead of on two competing branches. Majors land on their own major- branch and are not automerged.
Group web/ npm updates separately from .tektonic/

Group every container image — Dockerfiles, docker-compose, chart values and the .tektonic/ image tags from the customManager below — into one branch. Chainguard nginx was otherwise its own PR every day.

Re-synthesize .tekton/ on any branch that touches .tektonic/ — a @tektonic-ci/* bump, a tsx/typescript bump, or an image bump from the customManager below. .tekton/ itself is in ignorePaths, so this synth is the only thing that writes it. Without this the PR carries the new source but the old manifests, tekton-check fails it, and automerge never fires. Needs RENOVATE_ALLOWED_COMMANDS on the renovate-ocidex cronjob in homelab, or Renovate skips the commands. installTools because a regex-only (image) branch never installs node on its own. executionMode 'branch' runs the synth once over the final set of updates.

Hold web/ typescript at <7 (.tektonic/ is already on 7 and must keep getting updates): typescript-eslint (^8) peer-depends on typescript ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0", so TypeScript 7 fails npm install (ERESOLVE) and leaves the major-update PR perpetually red. This rule must also cover the eslint scope if that combination ever regresses — matchPackageNames matches the exact name, so a hold on "eslint" does not hold "@eslint/js". Lift once typescript-eslint peer-supports TypeScript 7.

customManagers.description: Bump base/tool image tags in the tektonic TypeScript source (.tektonic/**/*.ts); the postUpgradeTasks re-synth carries the bump into the generated .tekton/ YAML.
